brief.job: Determine whether Relay 3.4.0 changes an existing pipeline and find any required follow-up before upgrading.
brief.consequence: Missing a breaking change can stop a production release; treating every note as equally urgent slows routine maintenance.
facts: Breaking: the default artifact retention changed from 90 days to 30 days for new projects. Existing project retention is unchanged. Set retentionDays in relay.config.json to retain a different period.
Changed: relay deploy now fails before upload when the configured target is missing. The error names the missing target.
Added: relay deploy --dry-run prints the resolved target and artifact list without publishing.
Fixed: environment variables containing an equals sign are preserved in generated shell scripts.
Deprecated: relay init --legacy will be removed in Relay 4.0. Use relay init --format yaml instead.
The audience needs a readable distinction among breaking, changed, added, fixed, and deprecated notes, with a path to the related configuration reference. No migration guide URL is supplied.

required_interactions: Navigate to the configuration reference placeholder
acceptance_checks: A release engineer can identify the applicable breaking change and existing-project exception in one scan.
The page keeps a readable release narrative instead of becoming a card grid.
Every command, version, and behavioral claim matches the supplied facts.
